title: CLR/115/2014 of Smt Kumud AND ANOTHER Vs Mahant Govinddas Chela Late Maniram Das AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Civil Revision No. 115 of 2014
Smt. Kumud and another ...Revisionists.
Versus
Mahant Govinddas Chela late Maniram Das
and others ... Respondents
Present:
Mr. M.S. Tyagi, Advocate for the revisionists.
Mr. B.D. Pandey, Advocate for the respondents.
Dated: 7th November, 2017
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Though, in a suit, the plaintiff may not be having an
absolute right to file his replication to the written statement
but still it happens to be substantive right under Order 8
Rule 9 C.P.C. where the plaintiff has been granted the
liberty to file any subsequent pleading after filing the
written statement of the defendant. Such an application
would only be filed bringing on record the replication only
with the rider that it could be done with the leave of the
Court and in terms which the Court feels it to be
appropriate to adjudicate the case in a convenient manner.
In the present case, the defendant respondents filed
their written statement in a suit of the revisionist in August,
2011. The revisionist moved an application, paper No. 70-C
alongwith the replication to the written statement, though,
it was filed belatedly, on 26th July, 2014. The same has been
rejected by the learned Trial Court, by the impugned order
dated 11th August, 2014, only on the ground that the

2
revision was filed belatedly. Due to the rejection of the
application for taking the replication on record, it is the case
of the revisionist that a substantial right to place the
pleading on record in reply to the written statement has
been curtailed and he has been deprived of to effectively
participate in his own suit.
The delay itself cannot be a reason for rejecting an
application, whereby, a party to the litigation is deprived to
place his case in a complete and appropriate manner so as
to enable to put his pleadings on record before the learned
Trial Court.
In that view of the matter, the revision is allowed.
The impugned order is quashed. The revisionist's
application, paper No. 70-C, which she has preferred for
taking her replication on record, is allowed in terms of the
provision contained under Order 8 Rule 9 of the C.P.C.
No order as to costs.
Subject to the above, since the proceedings of the suit
is pending since 2011, the trial court is requested to expedite
the suit and decide the same as early as possible, without
inordinate delay and granting unnecessary adjournments.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
07.11.2017
Shiv
